title: LinkedIn profile checklist
intro: Twelve checks. Open your profile next to this page and tick each one as you fix it.

open.label: Open my profile
open.hint: Not opening in the app? In LinkedIn, tap your photo, then tap it again.

items.check: A clear head-and-shoulders photo of you
example: ✅ Face a window, plain light wall behind you, phone at eye level. Your face fills most of the square. Natural smile, eyes to the camera.
✅ A formal shirt, kurta or top is enough. You don’t need a blazer.
❌ Arm’s-length selfie, a wedding or function photo, a crop from a group picture, sunglasses, filters.
Cleaned up the background with an app? Fine. A changed face is not: it must look like you on interview day.
Test: shrink it to fingernail size. Still clearly you? That’s how it shows next to your request.
Use the same photo on Gmail and WhatsApp, so HR knows the mail and the call are the same person.

items.check: Your name exactly as on your CV, with nothing before it
example: ✅ Ananya Iyer: the same spelling as your CV, SSP and Gmail.
❌ CA Ananya Iyer · Semi CA Ananya · Ananya Iyer (CA Finalist) · Aspiring CA
Only ICAI members may put “CA” before their name. A partner who sees it on a CA Inter profile stops reading.
Your stage goes in the headline: “CA Inter cleared”. “CA Finalist” is a word you search with, not a title for your profile.

items.check: Headline: your stage, target, city and one proof
example: ✅ CA Inter cleared (September 2026), first attempt | Seeking articleship in statutory audit | Pune  ← my pick, if it’s true
✅ CA Inter cleared (Group I May 2026, Group II September 2026) | Seeking articleship in audit | Delhi NCR
✅ CA Inter cleared (May 2026) | ICITSS done | Seeking articleship in GST | Ahmedabad or Vadodara | GST Work Simulation
✅ CA Inter cleared (September 2026) | B.Com, [College] | Seeking articleship in direct tax | Bengaluru
✅ CA Inter result awaited (September 2026) | ICITSS done | Seeking articleship in audit | Kolkata
✅ CA Inter cleared (September 2026), AIR [n] | Seeking articleship in audit | Chennai  ← only with your rank letter
❌ Aspiring CA | Finance enthusiast | Learner: nothing anyone searches for.
❌ CA Finalist || Hardworking || Dedicated: a title you don’t hold yet, and words nobody types.

Your headline sits under your name everywhere: search results, their invitations, every comment. A partner decides from this one line whether to open your profile. HR search in words like “CA Inter” and the exam month. Put those words in, and you show up.
Test: search your own words (articleship statutory audit Pune) → People. Are you there? What do the headlines around you say?
Change it the day your status changes: result, ICITSS, selection.
items.copy: CA Inter cleared ([Month Year]) | Seeking articleship in [domain] | [City] | [one proof]

items.check: Your profile address is just your name
example: ✅ linkedin.com/in/ananya-iyer
Taken? Add an initial or your city: ananya-k-iyer, ananya-iyer-pune.
❌ The default with random characters (ananya-iyer-7b2c91a4), a nickname, your birth year.
How: your profile → Public profile & URL → edit your custom URL → Save.
Put it on your CV and in your Gmail signature behind the word “LinkedIn”. Then open it once from your CV on your phone.

items.check: About: the first three lines say who you are, what you’ve done and what you want
example: > I cleared CA Intermediate in September 2026 and I’m looking for articleship in statutory audit in Pune.
> In my Statutory audit Work Simulation I vouched 20 purchase bills against the PO, GRN and ledger and flagged 3 exceptions.
> I want to learn working papers in a team where seniors review my work. Write to me at ananya.iyer@email.com.
Only these lines show before “…see more”, and most people never click it. Line 1: your stage and target. Line 2: one thing you have actually done. Line 3: what you want to learn, and your email.
Write in “I”: short lines, a blank line after every two or three.
Helped a CA office or a family business? That’s your line 2: “For two months I helped a CA office prepare GSTR-1 and match purchase invoices with GSTR-2B for six clients.”

Result awaited? Start with “I’ve written CA Intermediate (September 2026), result awaited, and finished ICITSS.” Then a project: “I built an Excel bank reconciliation for a practice company and found 4 unmatched entries.”
After the three lines, if you like: how you used your exam break, one college role, and a last line of search words (Statutory audit · Vouching · Excel · Tally Prime).
❌ “Passionate, hardworking, dedicated professional”, hobbies copied from a sample, one long paragraph, “he” or “she” about yourself.
Only lines you can talk about for two minutes in an interview. Read it on your phone before you save.
items.copy:
I cleared CA Intermediate in [Month Year] and I’m looking for articleship in [domain] in [City].
[One thing you have actually done, with a number.]
I want to learn [what you want to learn]. Write to me at [your email].

items.check: ICAI and your college in Education, picked from the list so their logos show
example: How: Add profile section → Education → start typing “The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India” and pick it from the list. Don’t type it in full by hand.
Degree: CA Intermediate. Description: “Both groups cleared (September 2026) · ICITSS completed”, or one line per group with its month and year. Paper exemptions only if you got them.
Add CA Foundation as a second ICAI entry if you like. Add your college the same way: B.Com, years, “pursuing” if you haven’t finished.
Marks: the same figures as your CV, or leave them out. Never rounded up.
❌ ICAI under Experience. Studying at ICAI is not a job at ICAI.
Why: people who search by school (ICAI, your college) find you, and a logo makes the entry look real.

items.check: Every course and simulation you finished, under Licenses & certifications
example: e.g. Statutory audit Work Simulation, MSC Articleship Program · issuer My Student Club · Oct 2026
e.g. PwC US Audit Job Simulation · issuer Forage · Oct 2026
e.g. SEBI Investor Awareness Test (Level 1) · issuer NISM · Sep 2026

How: Add profile section → Recommended → Add licenses & certifications. Pick the issuer from the list so its logo shows. Issue date: the month you finished. Expiry: only if your certificate shows one. Credential ID and URL if your certificate has them. Add the certificate PDF as media.
Same names and months as your CV. An interviewer who sees an Excel certificate dated February will ask why your CV says you learnt Excel after your exams.
Only what you finished. A course you started goes on the day you complete it.

items.check: One piece of your own work pinned in Featured
example: Best: your Work Simulation work sample (the vouching sheet with your findings), an Excel reconciliation you built, or a short post where you explain one idea in your own words.
How: Add profile section → Recommended → Add featured → + → a document or a link. A post must be published before you can pin it.
Nothing to show yet? Post your result (below), pin it, and swap it for a work sample later.
Before you upload, delete your phone number, your address and any real person’s or client’s name.
One strong item beats five weak ones. Not your CV: it carries your phone number.
items.copy: Cleared CA Intermediate ([Month Year]). Two things that worked for me: [one study habit] and [one revision habit]. Thank you, [teacher’s name], for [one specific thing]. Next: articleship in [domain] in [City].

items.check: Three skills you can prove, each linked to where you used it
example: Open one real articleship opening in your domain and note the skills it asks for.
Pick three you can actually show, e.g. Vouching · Microsoft Excel · GST returns.
How: Add profile section → Core → Add skills, then tick the simulation, course or project where you used each one.
Use the opening’s own words in your headline and About too: for an audit team, “statutory audit”, not just “finance”.
❌ Teamwork, Communication, Leadership as your top three. Everyone has them; nobody searches for them.

items.check: Open to Work: articleship, your cities, your real start date, all members
example: How: your profile → Open to → Finding a new job.
Job titles: Article Assistant, Articled Assistant.
Locations: only cities you can reach for an interview.
Start date and availability: the real first day you can join. Never “immediately” unless it’s true.
Who can see it: All LinkedIn members. Partners and seniors who post openings don’t use LinkedIn’s recruiter tool, so “Recruiters only” hides you from the very people you’re writing to.
All members also puts the #OpenToWork frame on your photo. That’s fine: it tells a partner what you want before you say a word.
Expected salary: leave it blank.

While you’re there: Jobs → Preferences → Resumes and application data → Upload your CV PDF. LinkedIn keeps it for when you apply through LinkedIn. Don’t add your CV to your profile itself: your network can download it, phone number and all.

items.check: Email in Contact info, a plain banner, your phone number nowhere public
example: Contact info: your name-based Gmail, e.g. ananya.iyer@email.com. Your connections see it. Leave the phone field empty.

Banner: a plain colour, or one simple line such as “Statutory audit · Excel · Pune”. A real photo of you presenting (ICITSS, a college event) works too. Keep the left third empty: your photo sits on it.
❌ Your phone number on the banner or in About. Anyone can see it, and scam calls follow. HR who want to call will ask, or take it from your CV.
❌ Quotes, city skylines, logos of firms you don’t work at.

items.check: One recommendation from someone who has seen your work
example: Who: the ICITSS faculty member who saw your presentation, a coaching teacher, your college project guide, the CA or business owner you helped during a break. Not a friend, not a relative.
How: connect first. Then open their profile → More → Request a recommendation → how you know them and your role then → your message.
Give them the facts, so writing takes two minutes. Make “no” easy.
When it’s up: “Thank you so much, Sir/Ma’am. I’ve added it to my profile, and I’ll tell you where I join.”
❌ “I’ll write one for you if you write one for me.”
❌ Writing it yourself for them to paste.
items.copy: Hello Sir/Ma’am, I hope you’re well. I’m applying for articleship in [domain] and would be grateful for a short LinkedIn recommendation, if you’re comfortable writing one. In case it helps you recall: in [Month Year] I [presented the case on revenue recognition in your ICITSS batch]. Two or three lines are plenty. If you’re busy, no problem at all. Thank you, [Your name]

notes.title: Same story as your CV
notes.text: On a laptop: your profile → More → Save to PDF. Anyone can save your profile this way, HR included. Put it next to your CV and read line by line: result month and groups, marks, certificate months, projects, city. If your profile and your CV disagree, the interviewer believes neither.

notes.title: Experience: only real work
notes.text: No work yet? Leave Experience empty. Your Work Simulation and courses go under Licenses & certifications, never under Experience or Internship. Did real work in a CA office or a family business? Add it with what you did and how much: “Matched 120 purchase invoices with GSTR-2B for six clients; flagged 9 mismatches.”

done.title: Your profile is ready
done.text: Now find the people who decide. Open LinkedIn search links and start with this week’s posts in your city.
